To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 3He/3H yield ratio is a promising observable to study the nuclear symmetry energy in the density range from 2/3 ρ0 to ρ0, where ρ0 is the saturation density of symmetric nuclear matter, and that this observable is in qualitative agreement with the recent FOPI data.

the 3He/3H ratio is sensitive to nuclear matter properties in the sub-saturation density regime and that the FOPI data are consistent with the recent constraints on nuclear matter properties at sub-saturnation densities.

the yield ratio between the 3H and the 3He isotopes emitted in central collisions of heavy nuclei in the beam energy region of 0.12-1 GeV/n can be used as a sensitive probe of the nuclear equation of state at densities below normal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nuclear equation of state at sub- and supra-saturation densities, which is a crucial input in astrophysical models and in the understanding of the properties of compact objects.
the study of the symmetry energy at sub- and supra-saturation densities using the 3H+3He ratio and the elliptic flow as two sensitive probes.
the nuclear symmetry energy, which is one of the most fundamental nuclear properties, and the results obtained from the 3H+3He ratio and the elliptic flow are consistent with each other.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FOPI data on the 3H and/or 3He yields are consistent with both soft and stiff symmetry energy at low and high densities, respectively, but not with a linear one.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the FOPI data on the 3H and the 3He yields and their ratio as well as the elliptic flow data of free nucleons are consistent with a moderately soft to linear density dependence of the nuclear symmetry potential energy.
the UrQMD model with a density dependent Skyrme energy density functional is capable of describing simultaneously the elliptic flow and the 3H-3He ratio data for the 40Ca + Ca system.
both the high- and low-density symmetry energy can be constrained by the FOPI data on the elliptic flow and 3H/He ratios, respectively.
